a generalized Beth–Uhlenbek approach for mesons and diquraks in hot, dense QCD.
the thermodynamics of strongly interacting matter in the context of the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model and its extensions.
the thermodynamics of mesons and di-quarks at finite temperature and chemical potential.

the present Beth–Uhlenbek approach is an important step forward towards a realistic description of mesons and diquraks in hot, dense medium.
the generalized Beth–Uhlenbek equation is a very useful tool for the investigation of meson and diqaurk correlations in hot, dense, strongly interacting quark matter.
the Beth-Uhlenbeck approach to bound state dissociation is an important first step in a program of hadronizaton of chiral quarks models.

we have presented a first step towards a consistent description of the thermodynamic and transport properties of hadronic matter in chiral quark model approaches.
the Beth–Uhenbeck approach is a very useful and powerful tool for the description of bound state dissociations in hot, dense hadronic matter.

the Beth–Ulenbeck approach to meson and di-quark correlations is a powerful tool for the investigation of hadronization in dense and/or hot quark matter.
the Mott transition is a genuine feature of the thermodynamics of bound states in the Beth–Uhlenbeck approach.
